ROLE: Release the storage owned by a buffer and return it to the canonical empty state; safe to call repeatedly and after a failed reserve/append.

FUNC.NAME: buffer_init
FUNC.ROLE: Reset the fields after the release

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_init
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: no value; the buffer becomes empty (data NULL, len 0, cap 0)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases nothing; only field values are set
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions (NULL is accepted and ignored)

LOGIC.INPUT: buf, a caller-owned buffer, or NULL. Precondition: any storage reachable through buf->data was allocated by buffer_reserve/buffer_append and has not been transferred to another owner.
LOGIC.ACTION: If buf is NULL, return. Otherwise call free(buf->data) exactly once (free(NULL) is permitted and is the path taken by a buffer that never allocated storage), then set data = NULL, len = 0, cap = 0 by calling buffer_init(buf). The length is not simply cleared: the allocation itself is released so that no memory is retained after the call.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: The allocation is returned to the allocator and buf is empty; no value is returned.
INVARIANTS_USED: consume/shorten never frees storage, so free() must target buf->data, not a suffix
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: buf is NULL or holds a valid struct byte_buf; no aliasing owner of buf->data remains.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe; the caller owns the buffer exclusively.
